key_big: BEDMAS: brackets, exponents, then ÷ and × left to right, then + and − left to right.
key_sub: 2 + 3 × 4 = 14, not 20. 12 ÷ 2 × 3 = 18, not 2. With integers, use the sign rules at each step: (−3)² = 9 and 8 − (−6) = 14.
body_html:
Why the order matters

An expression with more than one operation could give different answers if people worked in a different order. So everyone uses the same order of operations. In BC classrooms it is remembered as BEDMAS.

StepDo thisExample
1Brackets(25 + 15) × 3 = 40 × 3 = 120
2Exponents (squares)3 + 4² = 3 + 16 = 19
3÷ and ×, as equals, from left to right12 ÷ 2 × 3 = 6 × 3 = 18
4+ and −, as equals, from left to right20 − 8 + 3 = 12 + 3 = 15

D and M are a team, and so are A and S

BEDMAS lists D before M, but division does not always come first. ÷ and × have the same rank, so do whichever comes first from the left. The same is true for + and −.

Brackets and a square

Evaluate (5 + 3)² − 10.

(5 + 3)² − 10 = 8² − 10 = 64 − 10 = 54.

Answer: 54

Integers and decimals

The order is the same with negative numbers and decimals. Use the integer sign rules at each step: two negatives multiplied or divided give a positive, and subtracting a negative is the same as adding.

Subtracting a negative

Evaluate 8 − (−2) × 3.

8 − (−2) × 3 = 8 − (−6) = 14. Subtracting −6 is the same as adding 6.

Answer: 14

Decimals

Evaluate 2.5 + 1.5 × 4.

2.5 + 1.5 × 4 = 2.5 + 6 = 8.5. Not 16: that adds first.

Answer: 8.5

Word problems as one expression

Write the whole problem as one expression, then use BEDMAS. Use brackets when a sum must be found before you multiply or divide.

Change from $20

Mei buys 3 bubble teas at $6.25 each and pays with a $20 bill. How much change does she get?

One expression: 20 − 3 × 6.25 = 20 − 18.75 = 1.25.

Answer: $1.25

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
2 + 3 × 4 = 5 × 4 = 20Multiply first: 2 + 12 = 14
12 ÷ 2 × 3 = 12 ÷ 6 = 2÷ and × are equals: left to right, 6 × 3 = 18
20 − 8 + 3 = 20 − 11 = 9+ and − are equals: left to right, 12 + 3 = 15
4² = 8A square is the number times itself: 4 × 4 = 16
(−3)² = −9(−3) × (−3) = 9. Two negatives give a positive
8 − (−6) = 2Subtracting a negative means adding: 8 + 6 = 14

faq.q: What is BEDMAS in Grade 7 math?
faq.a: BEDMAS is the order of operations used in Canada: Brackets, Exponents, Division and Multiplication (left to right), then Addition and Subtraction (left to right). For example, 2 + 3 × 4 = 2 + 12 = 14, not 20.

faq.q: Is BEDMAS the same as PEMDAS and BODMAS?
faq.a: Yes. PEMDAS (used in the US) and BODMAS (used in the UK) give the same order with different words. In all of them, × and ÷ have the same rank and so do + and −, so 12 ÷ 2 × 3 = 18.

faq.q: Where is order of operations in the BC Grade 7 math curriculum?
faq.a: It is in the Grade 7 Computational fluency standard: operations with integers, including the order of operations. Students also use it with decimals and fractions and when they write expressions for word problems.

faq.q: Does order of operations help with the Grade 7 FSA?
faq.a: Yes. The Grade 7 FSA numeracy section asks students to solve number problems, and many need more than one step. Writing a problem as one expression and using BEDMAS helps students get the steps in the right order.

items.q: In 6 × 4 + 18 ÷ 3, which operation do you do last?
items.e: 6 × 4 + 18 ÷ 3 = 24 + 18 ÷ 3 = 24 + 6 = 30. Do × and ÷ first (6 × 4 = 24 and 18 ÷ 3 = 6), then add. The order does matter: adding first gives 6 × 22 ÷ 3 = 44, a different answer.

sets.title: Decimals and word problems in one expression

items.q: A family takes BC Ferries to Vancouver Island. The fare is $62.50 for the car and $19.25 for each of the 4 people. What is the total fare?
items.e: One expression: 62.5 + 4 × 19.25. 62.5 + 4 × 19.25 = 62.5 + 77 = 139.5, so $139.50. Not $327: that charges the car fare 4 times. Not $81.75: that counts only one person. Not $77: that stops one step too early.

items.q: A Grade 7 class of 28 students goes to Grouse Mountain. Each student pays $15, and the class pays $45 for the bus. What is the total cost?
items.e: One expression: 28 × 15 + 45. 28 × 15 + 45 = 420 + 45 = 465, so $465. Not $1680: that comes from adding or subtracting before multiplying or dividing. Not $88: that adds all the numbers. Not $420: that stops one step too early.
5.8 + 2.7 × 2 = 5.8 + 5.4 = 11.2. Not 17: that comes from working left to right without doing × and ÷ first. Not 17.66: that uses the wrong pair of numbers.

items.q: At 6:00 a.m. the temperature in Prince George is −8°C. It rises 3°C every hour for 4 hours. What is the temperature at 10:00 a.m.?
items.e: One expression: (−8) + 3 × 4. (−8) + 3 × 4 = (−8) + 12 = 4, so 4°C. Not −20°C: that comes from working left to right without doing × and ÷ first. Not 12°C: that forgets the starting temperature. Not 20°C: that drops the minus sign on −8.

items.q: In a class quiz game, a correct answer scores 5 points and a wrong answer scores −3 points. Ji-woo gets 7 correct and 9 wrong. What is her score?
items.e: One expression: 7 × 5 + 9 × (−3). 7 × 5 + 9 × (−3) = 35 + 9 × (−3) = 35 + (−27) = 8, so 8 points. Not −132 points: that comes from working left to right without doing × and ÷ first. Not 62 points: that comes from a sign error: a negative and a positive multiplied or divided give a negative. Not 35 points: that stops one step too early.

items.q: At noon the temperature in Kamloops is 4°C. It drops 2°C every hour for 5 hours. Which expression gives the new temperature?
items.e: 4 − 5 × 2 = 4 − 10 = −6. So the new temperature is −6°C. (4 − 5) × 2 subtracts before multiplying. 5 × 2 − 4 subtracts in the wrong order and gives 6°C.
(2.4 + 3) × 2.5 = 5.4 × 2.5 = 13.5. Not 9.9: that comes from ignoring the brackets. Not 7.9: that adds instead of multiplying.

items.q: It rains 12.4 mm in Vancouver on Monday, 8.6 mm on Tuesday and 6.3 mm on Wednesday. What is the mean daily rainfall?
items.e: One expression: (12.4 + 8.6 + 6.3) ÷ 3. (12.4 + 8.6 + 6.3) ÷ 3 = (21 + 6.3) ÷ 3 = 27.3 ÷ 3 = 9.1, so 9.1 mm. Not 23.1 mm: that comes from ignoring the brackets. Not 81.9 mm: that multiplies instead of dividing. Not 27.3 mm: that stops one step too early.

items.q: Owen hikes 4.5 km to a lake in the Okanagan and 4.5 km back, plus a 2.4 km loop around the lake. How far does he hike in all?
items.e: One expression: 2 × 4.5 + 2.4. 2 × 4.5 + 2.4 = 9 + 2.4 = 11.4, so 11.4 km. Not 13.8 km: that comes from adding or subtracting before multiplying or dividing. Not 6.9 km: that forgets the walk back. Not 9 km: that stops one step too early.

items.q: Mei buys 3 bubble teas at $6.25 each. She pays with a $20 bill. How much change does she get?
items.e: One expression: 20 − 3 × 6.25. 20 − 3 × 6.25 = 20 − 18.75 = 1.25, so $1.25. Not $106.25: that comes from working left to right without doing × and ÷ first. Not $13.75: that pays for only one tea. Not $18.75: that stops one step too early.

items.q: A box lacrosse team of 12 players has 4 cases of 24 water bottles. They give 12 bottles to the coaches and share the rest equally among the players. How many bottles does each player get?
items.e: One expression: (4 × 24 − 12) ÷ 12. (4 × 24 − 12) ÷ 12 = (96 − 12) ÷ 12 = 84 ÷ 12 = 7, so 7 bottles. Not 95 bottles: that comes from ignoring the brackets. Not 84 bottles: that forgets to share among the players. Not 9 bottles: that adds the coaches’ bottles instead of taking them away.

4 × 2.75 − 2.25 = 11 − 2.25 = 8.75. Not 2: that comes from adding or subtracting before multiplying or dividing. Not 13.25: that uses the wrong sign.
